subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human instruction provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, outbound messaging, gateway mutations, and autonomous agent actions?
rationale: This would create a new security boundary, public/plugin-facing policy context, config shape, and compatibility behavior, so source inspection cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Core gateway policy
options.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the gateway/tool boundary.

options.title: Plugin facts first
options.body: First land additive hook/action/provenance facts so trusted security plugins can implement the policy before core owns enforcement.

options.title: Fold into taint umbrella
options.body: Defer this into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers settle one unified model.

recommendation.title: Core gateway policy
recommendation.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the gateway/tool boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current evidence connects this account to hook contracts and exec approval policy seams where the public contract would likely be shaped.
